claim: The same rounded surface recurrence statistic can be generated by substantially different higher-order sequence processes.
A fixed neural step function can be iterated by rereading its own discrete output, and transplanting a donor hidden state transfers the donor successor under an unchanged readout.

Across recurrent and attention architectures, identical current visible inputs can yield different outputs when formation history differs. Hidden-motion diagnostics are retained as a secondary measurement rather than a required gate.
A learned same-task/opposite-drift mirror can be used as a state correction surface that reduces long-run output deviation under repeated shocks relative to free dynamics and an unrelated mirror.

A source-specific warning works when failure is generated by the monitored takeover mechanism, loses coverage when a new noise source generates failure, and regains discrimination after that residual source is represented explicitly.
Two opposite structural factorizations can generate the same observational Gaussian geometry; an intervention response distinguishes the candidate causal worlds.
On the same complete compositional task, recurrent and attention architectures all develop non-additive interactions concentrated on the fragment pairs that define the target computation.

A mode direction discovered on one paired cohort and frozen on a development cohort causally shifts first-action logits in both directions on a new confirmation cohort, with matched orthogonal controls.

Answer readiness along a recurrent trajectory is non-monotonic; stopping at a ready state and applying a bounded state-aware recovery action after a bad transition outperform unconditional continuation in the same controlled system.
Holding the task and architecture fixed, adding an early auxiliary relation loss changes the geometry of the early bottleneck while retaining exact final-task performance.

For a two-stage routed computation, forcing the wrong early expert damages the intermediate prediction, while a correctly routed downstream recomputation can recover most of that damage; forcing the downstream route wrong removes that recovery.
